explain.narrative:
## Capstone: Command-Line Task Manager

Separate task data, application logic, persistence and console interaction. Build one feature at a time and test empty storage, duplicate IDs, invalid commands and file errors.

Identify the input and desired result. Select the Java construct or API that supports the requirement. Keep code readable, handle documented failures and state assumptions clearly.

Compile with JDK 21, predict output before running, and test normal, boundary and invalid inputs.

examples.title: Core API
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { record Task(int id, String title, boolean done) {} Task t = new Task(1, "Write tests", false); System.out.println(t.title()); } }
examples.explanation: Models a task as an immutable record.

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { java.util.List<String> tasks = new java.util.ArrayList<>(); tasks.add("Plan"); tasks.add("Build"); System.out.println(tasks); } }
examples.explanation: Stores tasks in an ordered list.

examples.title: Boundary behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { java.util.Map<Integer,String> tasks = new java.util.LinkedHashMap<>(); tasks.put(1, "Review"); System.out.println(tasks.containsKey(1)); } }
examples.explanation: Uses a stable ID to look up a task.

examples.title: Alternative pattern
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { String command = "complete"; System.out.println(switch(command) { case "add", "list", "complete" -> "known command"; default -> "unknown command"; }); } }
examples.explanation: Validates a command before dispatching an action.

examples.title: Verify the result
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { java.nio.file.Path p = java.nio.file.Files.createTempFile("tasks", ".txt"); try { java.nio.file.Files.writeString(p, "1|Plan|false"); System.out.println(java.nio.file.Files.readString(p)); } finally { java.nio.file.Files.deleteIfExists(p); } } }
examples.explanation: Demonstrates a simple persistence record; a production project should validate fields and handle escaping.

practise.guidedTask: Model a Task with an ID, title and completion state. Implement add, list and complete commands using a Map and reject duplicate IDs.
practise.independentTask: Build the command-line task manager with separate Task, TaskService, TaskRepository and Main classes. Persist tasks in a documented UTF-8 text format.
hints: Choose the API that matches the data representation and operation.
Test empty, normal and failure cases; verify exact output or file contents.
practise.challenge: Test empty storage, malformed records, duplicate IDs, unknown commands, completing a missing task and restarting after saved changes.
